paper.title: Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandit and Its Extension to Probabilistically Triggered Arms

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial multi-armed bandit (CMAB) with probabilistically triggered arms
unmapped: Nonlinear expected reward r_mu(S) satisfying monotonicity and bounded smoothness with function f
Base arms outside the played super arm may be probabilistically triggered (minimum triggering probability p_i); feedback is outcomes of all triggered arms
Access to an (alpha,beta)-approximation oracle (not a linear optimization oracle; oracle field is approximate)
Outcomes of different base arms may be dependent within a round
settings.definition_quote: A combinatorial multi-armed bandit (CMAB) problem consists of m base arms associated with a set of random variables X_{i,t} ... with bounded support on [0,1]. ... The outcomes of base arms in S may trigger other base arms not in S to be played ... Reg^A_{\bp,\alpha,\beta}(n) = n \alpha \beta \opt_{\bp} - \E_S[\sum_{t=1}^n r_\bp(S^A_t)].

symbols.Delta_min_i: smallest gap alpha*opt - r(S) among bad super arms whose triggering set contains base arm i
symbols.ell_n_min_i: sampling threshold ell_n(Delta_min_i, p_i) = max(12 ln n/((f^{-1}(Delta))^2 p), 24 ln n/p) if p<1, 6 ln n/(f^{-1}(Delta))^2 if p=1
symbols.Int_ell_i: integral of ell_n(x,p_i) dx from Delta_min_i to Delta_max_i
symbols.p_i: minimum nonzero triggering probability of base arm i

conditions: expected reward satisfies monotonicity and bounded smoothness with function f
sum over base arms with K_i>0
tuning: UCB radius sqrt(3 ln t/(2 T_i)) truncated at 1

source.label: thm:cucb individual
source.quote: The $(\alpha,\beta)$-approximation regret of the CUCB algorithm in $n$ rounds using an $(\alpha,\beta)$-approximation oracle is at most \sum_{i\in [m], K_i>0} (\ell_n(\Delta^i_{\min},p_i) \Delta^i_{\min} + \int ... ) + ((2+\I\{p^* < 1\})\pi^2/6 +1) m \Delta_{\max}

results.notes: Quantity is (alpha,beta)-approximation regret (defined via expected rewards), recorded as 'other'. Delta_max is max gap over bad super arms. Text applications (PMC: sum 12|E|^2 ln n/Delta_min^i + (pi^2/3+1)|E|Delta_max; linear rewards: sum 12 a_max^2 L^2 ln n/Delta_min^i + ...; influence maximization: sum 24|V|^2|E|^2 ln n/(Delta_min^i p_i) + (pi^2/2+1)|E|Delta_max) are derived from this theorem; classical MAB gives sum 6 ln n/Delta_i + (pi^2/3+1) m Delta_max.

symbols.gamma_f: constant gamma in bounded smoothness function f(x)=gamma x^omega
symbols.omega: exponent in f(x)=gamma x^omega, omega in (0,1]

conditions: bounded smoothness function f(x) = gamma*x^omega with gamma>0, omega in (0,1]
tuning: UCB radius sqrt(3 ln t/(2 T_i))

source.label: thm:worstbound
source.quote: If the bounded smoothness function $f(x) = \gamma \cdot x^\omega$ for some $\gamma >0$ and $\omega\in (0,1]$, the regret of CUCB is at most: \frac{2\gamma}{2-\omega}(6m\ln n)^{\omega/2} n^{1-\omega/2}+(\frac{\pi^2}{3}+1) m \Delta_{\max}, if p^*=1

results.notes: Distribution-independent (alpha,beta)-approximation regret. For omega=1 gives O(sqrt(m n ln n)) for classical MAB; text applications: PMC sqrt(24|E|^3 n ln n)+..., linear a_max L sqrt(24 m n ln n)+...

symbols.p_i: minimum nonzero triggering probability of base arm i

conditions: bounded smoothness function f(x) = gamma*x^omega with gamma>0, omega in (0,1]
tuning: UCB radius sqrt(3 ln t/(2 T_i))
results.notes: Influence maximization application in text: |V| sqrt(48|E|^3 n ln n/p*) + (pi^2/2+1)|E|Delta_max.
